CASE-5.title: REL-034 out-of-hours escalation
CASE-5.text: Release REL-034, out-of-hours escalation. After two night-time chiller faults at Harbor View Medical Center, Lina Farah, Omar Saleh, Dana Khoury and Karim Aziz agree four requirements on Monday 7 December 2026. (1) Omar's agents need an "Escalate to on-call" command on the Case form. It must ask for confirmation, call the existing custom API cedar_EscalateCase (an action bound to incident with the output EscalationId) and show the result without leaving the form. The API's plug-in queues the page for the Azure Function OnCallPager (func-cedar-ops-prod), which calls the paging provider and logs each failure as the custom event EscalationFailed with the case number to the Application Insights resource appi-cedar-prod. (2) Cedar Night Desk, an internal ASP.NET Core web app for night supervisors, must let the signed-in supervisor ask the published Copilot Studio agent Cedar Service Assistant questions; answers must be limited to what that supervisor may see. (3) CedarReports, the Azure SQL reporting database, keeps a copy of all cases including the escalation columns. Its loader runs every 15 minutes, must also remove deleted cases, and is paused for up to three days during quarterly maintenance. (4) Lina must be told within 10 minutes when more than five pages fail within 15 minutes, with the failed case numbers.

sections.title: Section 2: goal set (invoice-status import)
sections.problem: Every night CedarLedger exports about 180,000 invoice-status changes that a .NET 10 console job (ServiceClient, application user) writes to the standard table Invoice status (cedar_invoicestatus, alternate key cedar_invoicenumber). Last night the job ran four hours, single-threaded, one UpdateRequest per row, and about 300 rows failed because their invoice number didn't exist yet. Goal: finish within 90 minutes, create rows whose invoice number doesn't exist, and never let one bad row stop the others.

items.stem: Sami's coordinators must not be able to set a work order to Completed unless at least one note with an image is attached to it. Work orders are updated from the Work order – Dispatch form, by the FieldLink sync through the Web API and by two cloud flows. What should Karim implement?

options.A: A client script on the form's OnSave event that cancels the save when no image note exists.
options.B: An automated cloud flow on modify that sets the status back to In progress when no image note exists.
options.C: A synchronous plug-in step on Update of Work order (filtering column: status), PreValidation stage, that queries the notes and throws InvalidPluginExecutionException when no image is attached.
options.D: A business rule with scope Entity that shows an error on the status column when no image note exists.

items.signal: "every channel" (form, Web API, flows) and "must not be able to": enforcement on the server, before the save.
items.why: Only server-side logic runs for every channel. A synchronous step in PreValidation (or PreOperation) can query related notes and cancel the operation with a message, so the row is never saved as Completed.

distractors.A: A form script only runs in the form; the FieldLink sync and the flows never load it.
distractors.B: The flow runs after the save: the row is Completed for a while and other systems may already have reacted to it.
distractors.D: Entity-scope business rules run on the server, but they can only test columns of the row itself; they can't query related notes.

items.stem: On the Site – Cedar form, a handler registered on the OnChange event of Site type (Pass execution context as first parameter is ticked) must show the section sec_access on tab tab_general only for hospitals and show the selected Site type label in a form notification. Which code is correct?

options.A: const f = Xrm.Page; f.ui.tabs.get("tab_general").sections.get("sec_access").setVisible(isHospital);
options.B: const f = executionContext.getFormContext(); f.ui.tabs.get("tab_general").sections.get("sec_access").setVisible(isHospital); f.ui.setFormNotification(f.getAttribute("cedar_sitetype").getText(), "INFO", "sitetype");
options.C: const f = executionContext.getFormContext(); f.getAttribute("sec_access").setVisible(isHospital); f.ui.setFormNotification(f.getAttribute("cedar_sitetype").getValue(), "INFO", "sitetype");
options.D: document.getElementById("sec_access").style.display = isHospital ? "block" : "none";

items.signal: "Pass execution context" and "label": formContext from the execution context, UI through tabs and sections, getText for a choice label.
items.why: getFormContext() is the supported entry point. Sections are reached through ui.tabs and tab.sections; getText returns the label of the selected choice, getValue its number.

distractors.A: Xrm.Page is deprecated; use the form context passed to the handler.
distractors.C: A section isn't an attribute, and getValue returns the choice number, not its label.
distractors.D: Direct DOM access is unsupported and breaks when the form markup changes.

items.stem: A plug-in must stop a Case from being created when the customer account is on credit hold. The check uses only the submitted values and must run before the database transaction starts, so no other synchronous step does work that has to be rolled back. In which stage should Karim register the step?

options.A: PostOperation, asynchronous.
options.B: PreOperation, synchronous.
options.C: MainOperation, synchronous.
options.D: PreValidation, synchronous.

items.signal: "before the database transaction starts" and "stop": the only synchronous stage outside the transaction.
items.why: PreValidation (stage 10) runs before the transaction and can cancel the operation by throwing InvalidPluginExecutionException. PreOperation (20) also cancels, but inside the transaction.

distractors.A: An asynchronous step runs after the commit and can't cancel anything.
distractors.B: It can cancel, but it runs inside the transaction, which the stem rules out.
distractors.C: MainOperation (30) is used by custom APIs and virtual table providers, not for steps on Create.

items.stem: Keystone Audit, Cedar's safety auditor, wants a copy of every new Case within minutes. Its API is a simple HTTPS endpoint (about 40 cases a week) that authenticates with a key in an HTTP header and is rarely down for more than a few minutes. Dana wants no new Azure resources and no code outside Dataverse. Which option should Karim recommend?

options.A: An asynchronous webhook step on Create of Case, authentication HttpHeader with the key.
options.B: A Service Bus queue endpoint and an Azure Function that forwards each message to Keystone.
options.C: An Event Hubs endpoint that Keystone reads with its own consumer group.
options.D: A synchronous webhook step on Create of Case, authentication HttpHeader with the key.

items.signal: "simple HTTPS endpoint", "low volume", "rarely down", "no Azure resources".
items.why: A webhook needs no Azure resources; an asynchronous step doesn't delay the save and is retried as a system job when the endpoint is briefly unavailable. The key travels in a header.

distractors.B: It works, but Dana ruled out new Azure resources and code outside Dataverse.
distractors.C: Event Hubs is for high-volume streams with replay; it adds Azure resources for a trickle of cases.
distractors.D: A synchronous webhook makes every case save wait for Keystone and fails the save when Keystone is down.

items.stem: Karim's job changes a work order's Scheduled for and links it to the subcontractor account through the Web API. Another process may have changed the row since the job read it; such a change must not be overwritten silently. Which two parts belong in the request?

options.A: PATCH [org]/api/data/v9.2/cedar_workorders(<id>) with the header If-Match: *
options.B: PATCH [org]/api/data/v9.2/cedar_workorders(<id>) with the header If-Match: W/"<etag read earlier>"
options.C: "cedar_subcontractor": "<account id>" in the body
options.D: "cedar_Subcontractor@odata.bind": "/accounts(<account id>)" in the body
options.E: PUT [org]/api/data/v9.2/cedar_workorders(<id>) with the whole row in the body

items.signal: "must not be overwritten": optimistic concurrency with the ETag; "link to an account": a navigation property with @odata.bind.
items.why: If-Match with the ETag read earlier makes Dataverse answer 412 Precondition Failed when the row changed in between. A lookup is set through the single-valued navigation property (the lookup's schema name) and @odata.bind with the entity set path.

distractors.A: If-Match: * only prevents an upsert from creating a row; it doesn't detect changes by others.
distractors.C: A lookup can't be set through its logical name in the body; use the navigation property with @odata.bind.
distractors.E: PUT updates a single property in the Web API; sending the whole row would overwrite columns the job doesn't own.

items.stem: Karim's field control cedar.SignaturePad must store the signature as text in a Multiple lines of text column and use the device camera to photograph a paper signature when the device supports it; on desktops the control must still load. Which two manifest entries should he use?

options.A: <property name="signature" of-type="Multiple" usage="bound" required="true" />
options.B: <property name="signature" of-type="SingleLine.Text" usage="input" />
options.C: <feature-usage><uses-feature name="Device.captureImage" required="false" /></feature-usage>
options.D: <external-service-usage enabled="true"><domain>camera</domain></external-service-usage>

items.signal: "stores" (bound, Multiple) and "when the device supports it" (feature declared, not required).
items.why: A bound property of type Multiple reads and writes the column. Device features must be declared in feature-usage; required="false" lets the control load where the feature is missing, so the code checks before using it.

distractors.B: An input property is read-only for the control, and SingleLine.Text doesn't match a multi-line column.
distractors.D: external-service-usage declares external web domains (premium in canvas apps); it has nothing to do with the camera.
distractors.E: required="true" makes the control depend on the camera, which desktops don't offer.

items.stem: Finance insists that CedarLedger (Azure SQL) stays the system of record for invoices: no copies in Dataverse. Maya wants the account form to list each customer's invoices in a subgrid, with a view sorted by due date. Which approach should Karim propose?

options.A: An elastic table loaded nightly from CedarLedger.
options.B: A virtual table over CedarLedger with the SQL Server virtual connector provider, related to account and shown in a subgrid.
options.C: A standard table kept current by an hourly cloud flow.
options.D: A custom connector called from a canvas app embedded in the account form.

items.signal: "system of record", "no copies", "subgrid and view": a virtual table.
items.why: A virtual table presents external rows as a Dataverse table without storing them, so model-driven views and subgrids work while CedarLedger remains the only copy.

distractors.A: Elastic tables store data in Dataverse: a copy, and a stale one.
distractors.C: Another copy, up to an hour old, plus a flow to maintain.
distractors.D: It avoids a copy but replaces a standard subgrid and view with a custom app: far more to build than needed.

items.stem: The nightly job cedar-automation authenticates with a certificate and works in Cedar-Dev. In Cedar-Test it gets a token for https://<cedar-test>.crm.dynamics.com/.default without errors, but every Dataverse call fails with "The user is not a member of the organization." What should Karim do?

options.A: Add the Dynamics CRM user_impersonation API permission to the app registration and grant admin consent.
options.B: Request the token for the Cedar-Dev URL instead.
options.C: Create an application user for cedar-automation in Cedar-Test and give it the Cedar Automation security role.
options.D: Assign the app registration the Contributor role on the Azure subscription.

items.signal: Token issued, then "not a member of the organization": Dataverse doesn't know this identity in this environment.
items.why: Application users are per environment. The token is valid; Dataverse refuses it because no application user exists for the app in Cedar-Test. Creating one with a least-privilege role fixes it.

distractors.A: user_impersonation is a delegated permission for user tokens; it never authorises an app-only identity in Dataverse.
distractors.B: A token for another environment would fail with 401; the token isn't the problem.
distractors.D: Azure roles don't grant access to Dataverse.

items.stem: The Dispatch Planner code app must start the flow "Cedar – Notify subcontractor" when a coordinator selects Send, passing the work order number. Which flow can the app call?

options.A: An automated cloud flow with the Dataverse trigger "When a row is added, modified or deleted".
options.B: A scheduled cloud flow that runs every five minutes.
options.C: An instant flow with the Power Apps trigger that isn't in a solution, shared with the coordinators.
options.D: A solution-aware instant flow with the Power Apps trigger, added to the app with the CLI and regenerated when its inputs change.

items.signal: "code app calls a flow": only solution-aware instant flows with the Power Apps trigger can be added.
items.why: Code apps add flows that are solution-aware and use the Power Apps trigger; the CLI generates a typed service, which must be regenerated after the flow's inputs change. The flow runs with its connection references.

distractors.A: An automated flow starts from its own trigger; a code app can't call it.
distractors.B: A scheduled flow can't be called from an app.
distractors.C: The trigger is right, but flows outside a solution can't be added to a code app.

items.stem: A synchronous PostOperation plug-in on Update of Case must write a timeline note when Priority changes from Normal to High, stating the old and the new value. What should Karim register and read?

options.A: A pre-image with the alias PreImage containing only prioritycode; compare it with prioritycode in the Target.
options.B: A post-image with all columns; compare it with the Target.
options.C: No image: retrieve the case inside the plug-in to get the old priority.
options.D: No image: read the old priority from the Target.

items.signal: "old and new value" on Update: a pre-image for the old value, the Target for the new one.
items.why: A pre-image holds the stored values before the operation; register it with an alias and only the needed columns. The Target holds the submitted (new) value.

distractors.B: A post-image holds the values after the update, so the old value is lost; all columns also cost performance.
distractors.C: In PostOperation a retrieve returns the new value, and it adds a call that an image avoids.
distractors.D: The Target contains only the submitted columns with their new values.

items.stem: Two new components: (1) the Azure Function SiteImport runs nightly without a user and writes Site rows; (2) the Dispatch Planner code app must show only the work orders the signed-in coordinator is allowed to see. Dana wants no stored secrets. Which two designs meet the requirements?

options.A: SiteImport uses its managed identity, with an application user in each environment holding the least-privilege role Cedar Site Import.
options.B: SiteImport uses an app registration with a client secret stored in the function's app settings.
options.C: The code app reads work orders through the signed-in user's Dataverse connection, so the user's security roles decide which rows are returned.
options.D: The code app reads through one shared service-account connection and filters rows by owner in code.
options.E: The SiteImport application user gets System Administrator so that imports never fail on privileges.

items.signal: "no user", "no stored secrets" → managed identity; "only rows the signed-in user may see" → delegated access as that user.
items.why: Name the identity at each hop: an unattended function uses a managed identity mapped to an application user with only the privileges it needs; an interactive app runs as the signed-in user so Dataverse security filters rows.

distractors.B: A client secret is a stored secret, which Dana ruled out; a managed identity removes it.
distractors.D: Filtering in code bypasses Dataverse security, and the shared account sees everything.
distractors.E: Far more privilege than writing Site rows needs.

items.stem: FieldLink sends job updates identified by the FieldLink job ID, which is the alternate key cedar_fieldlinkid on Work order. Work orders are always created in Cedar first; an update for an unknown job ID must fail and must not create a row. Which Web API request should the receiver send?

options.A: PATCH cedar_workorders(cedar_fieldlinkid='FL-2291') with no conditional header.
options.B: POST cedar_workorders with cedar_fieldlinkid in the body.
options.C: PATCH cedar_workorders(cedar_fieldlinkid='FL-2291') with the header If-Match: *
options.D: PATCH cedar_workorders(cedar_fieldlinkid='FL-2291') with the header If-None-Match: *

items.signal: "must not create a row" for an unknown key: update only.
items.why: A PATCH by alternate key is an upsert unless you add If-Match: *, which makes it update-only: an unknown key returns 404 and nothing is created.

distractors.A: Without a condition, PATCH upserts and creates a work order for an unknown job.
distractors.B: POST always creates; with an existing key it fails with a duplicate error.
distractors.D: If-None-Match: * means create only: it fails with 412 for existing rows, the normal case here.

items.stem: On Work order – Dispatch, the Subcontractor lookup must list only accounts whose service line matches the work order's service line, and the filter must follow later changes of the service line. Where and how should Karim register the filter?

options.A: In the form OnLoad handler (registered in the designer with Pass execution context), call getControl("cedar_subcontractor").addPreSearch(filterFn) once; filterFn reads the current service line and calls addCustomFilter.
options.B: Register filterFn on the lookup's PreSearch event in the form designer's Events tab.
options.C: In the service line OnChange handler, call addPreSearch(filterFn) each time the value changes.
options.D: In OnLoad, call addOnChange on the service line and then setValue on it, so that the OnChange handler applies the filter.

items.signal: "lookup filter" (PreSearch is code-only) and "follows later changes" (read the value when the lookup opens).
items.why: PreSearch handlers are added in code. Registering once in OnLoad and reading the current service line inside the handler keeps the filter current without stacking handlers.

distractors.B: The designer doesn't offer PreSearch; it's registered with addPreSearch.
distractors.C: Each change adds another handler; the filters pile up unless removePreSearch is called.
distractors.D: setValue doesn't fire OnChange, and the filter belongs to PreSearch anyway.

items.stem: The custom API cedar_RecalculateContracts takes about 90 seconds. Karim's Python caller times out waiting for the HTTP response. Lina wants the caller freed at once and told the outcome later; a preview feature is acceptable in Cedar-Test. What should Karim do?

options.A: Raise the caller's HTTP timeout to five minutes.
options.B: Send the request with the header Prefer: respond-async, keep the Location URL from the 202 response and poll it, or subscribe to OnBackgroundOperationComplete.
options.C: Register the custom API's plug-in step as asynchronous.
options.D: Move the logic to an asynchronous plug-in and raise the sandbox limit to ten minutes in the environment settings.

items.signal: "freed at once", "outcome later", "custom API": a background operation (preview).
items.why: With Prefer: respond-async, Dataverse accepts the request with 202 and a Location status monitor; the outcome is read later by polling, from the backgroundoperations table, a callback URL or the OnBackgroundOperationComplete event. It doesn't extend the plug-in's 2-minute limit.

distractors.A: The caller still waits, which is exactly what Lina wants to avoid.
distractors.C: The main operation of a custom API runs in its own stage; an asynchronous step returns nothing to the caller.
distractors.D: There is no setting that raises the sandbox's 2-minute limit.

items.stem: Karim adds the Dataverse table cedar_workorder to the Dispatch Planner code app as a data source. Which statement about it is correct?

options.A: It needs the connection ID of a shared service connection.
options.B: It can run FetchXML queries for aggregates.
options.C: It runs as the signed-in user, so each coordinator's security roles decide which rows the app returns.
options.D: It supports polymorphic lookups such as Customer on Case.

items.signal: Dataverse data source in a code app: no connection ID, signed-in user.
items.why: A Dataverse data source in a code app needs no connection ID and runs as the signed-in user. Polymorphic lookups, table-definition operations, FetchXML and alternate keys are listed as not yet supported.

distractors.A: Dataverse tables are added without a connection ID; there is no shared service connection.
distractors.B: FetchXML is on the "not yet supported" list for code apps.
distractors.D: Polymorphic lookups are on the "not yet supported" list.

items.stem: Makers' cloud flows must call cedar_GetSiteRisk with the input SiteCode (text) and receive RiskScore (whole number). The operation doesn't change data. How should Karim define the custom API?

options.A: A function (Is Function = Yes), unbound, Is Private = Yes so only flows can see it.
options.B: A function bound to the Site table.
options.C: A custom process action with the same parameters.
options.D: An action (Is Function = No), unbound, request parameter SiteCode of type String, response property RiskScore of type Integer, and an execute privilege to control who can call it.

items.signal: "called from cloud flows": flows call actions only, even for read-only work.
items.why: Functions use GET and can't be called from flows; an action can be read-only too. Access is controlled with an execute privilege, not by hiding the API.

distractors.A: Flows can't call functions, and Is Private only hides the API from metadata; it isn't security.
distractors.B: Still a function, so flows can't call it; binding adds nothing here.
distractors.C: Custom process actions are the older way; custom APIs are recommended for new operations.

items.stem: Sami wants a signature pad on the Work order and Case forms, bound to a text column, reused on both tables and shipped in CedarServiceCore. Which user-experience option should Karim choose?

options.A: A code app opened from a button on the form.
options.B: A generative page added to the app's navigation.
options.C: An HTML web resource placed in an iframe section of each form.
options.D: A code component (PCF) field control bound to the column and added to both forms.

items.signal: "on the form", "bound to a column", "reused": a PCF field control.
items.why: A PCF field control replaces how one column is shown and edited, is bound to it, can be added to any form and travels in the solution.

distractors.A: A code app is a standalone app, not a control inside a form.
distractors.B: A generative page is a page in the app, not a control bound to a column.
distractors.C: A web resource in an iframe isn't bound to the column and needs custom plumbing; PCF is the supported reusable control.

items.stem: FieldLink now requires the header X-FieldLink-Tenant: cedar on every call. Thirty flows use the FieldLink Jobs custom connector, and Lina doesn't want any of them changed. What should Karim add to the connector?

options.A: Custom code that adds the header to every request.
options.B: A Set HTTP header policy with the value cedar, applied to all operations.
options.C: A new connection parameter that each connection owner fills in.
options.D: An Azure Function in front of FieldLink that adds the header.

items.signal: "every call", "a fixed header", "no flow changed": a GA policy template.
items.why: Set HTTP header is a generally available template that adds or changes a header on the request at runtime, declaratively; with no operations listed it applies to all.

distractors.A: Code works but adds a script to maintain for something a template does declaratively.
distractors.C: Every connection would have to be edited, and the value is the same for everyone.
distractors.D: A new Azure resource for one header.

items.stem: The flow "Cedar – Notify on high priority" uses the Dataverse trigger "When a row is added, modified or deleted" (Modified, Case) and runs about 3,000 times a day. It should run only when a case is saved with Priority High. Which trigger configuration should Karim use?

options.A: Select columns: prioritycode; Filter rows: prioritycode eq 1.
options.B: No trigger settings; the first action is a Condition on prioritycode.
options.C: A trigger condition that compares the previous and the new value of prioritycode.
options.D: Filter rows: prioritycode eq 1 only.

items.signal: "only when … Priority High": filter in the trigger so no run is created.
items.why: Select columns limits the trigger to requests that include prioritycode; Filter rows evaluates the saved row (High is 1). Together they avoid thousands of empty runs. Note that a request that includes the column fires even if the value didn't change.

distractors.B: A run is created for every modification and only then stops; it costs runs and history.
distractors.C: The trigger has no previous values to compare.
distractors.D: It fires for every change of any column while the case is High.

items.stem: Karim's field control cedar.Rating shows stars bound to cedar_satisfaction. He calls notifyOutputChanged at the end of updateView, and the form freezes after the first click. What fixes it?

options.A: Render only in init and leave updateView empty.
options.B: Call notifyOutputChanged from getOutputs.
options.C: Wrap the notifyOutputChanged call in updateView in setTimeout.
options.D: Call notifyOutputChanged only from the click handler registered in init, and keep updateView for rendering from the context.

items.signal: "notifyOutputChanged in updateView" and "freezes": a render loop.
items.why: notifyOutputChanged makes the framework call getOutputs and then updateView again. Raising it from updateView loops. Raise it when the user changes the value; updateView only renders.

distractors.A: The control would never show values changed elsewhere on the form.
distractors.B: getOutputs is called because of notifyOutputChanged; calling it from there loops too.
distractors.C: It delays the loop, it doesn't remove it.

items.stem: The flow "Cedar – Close stale cases" runs on a "Connect with service principal" connection for the Dataverse connector. In Cedar-Test it fails with "Principal user (Id=…, type=8) is missing prvWriteIncident privilege". What should Karim change?

options.A: Share Omar's personal Dataverse connection with the flow instead.
options.B: Add Write on Case at the needed access level to the application user's role Cedar Automation.
options.C: Add the Dynamics CRM user_impersonation API permission to the app registration and grant admin consent.
options.D: Assign the System Administrator role to the application user.

items.signal: "missing prv… privilege": a Dataverse security role of the application user.
items.why: The identity is authenticated and known to Dataverse; it lacks one privilege. Add that privilege, at the needed depth, to the least-privilege role of the application user.

distractors.A: It removes the application identity Lina asked for and runs as Omar.
distractors.C: Entra API permissions don't authorise an app-only identity in Dataverse; roles do.
distractors.D: It works, but grants far more than one privilege.

items.stem: When a case is escalated to High, Dana wants a Teams message to the on-call coordinator and a follow-up task. No agent is involved, makers will maintain it, and it must ship in CedarServiceCore. What should Karim build?

options.A: An automated Power Automate cloud flow with the Dataverse trigger, in the solution.
options.B: A Copilot Studio agent flow with the same steps.
options.C: A Copilot Studio workflow on the GitHub Copilot harness.
options.D: A classic Dataverse background workflow.

items.signal: "no agent involved", "fixed steps": a cloud flow.
items.why: Fixed automation without an agent belongs in a Power Automate cloud flow. Agent flows are tools for agents and consume Copilot Studio capacity; workflows on the GitHub Copilot harness are for agentic work.

distractors.B: Agent flows exist to serve agents and are billed as Copilot Studio capacity; no agent is involved.
distractors.C: Agentic orchestration for a fixed two-step automation.
distractors.D: Classic workflows are legacy; cloud flows are the current option.

items.stem: The Dispatch Planner code app must call the FieldLink status API at https://api.fieldlink.example from the browser and may be embedded only in Cedar's intranet at https://intranet.cedarservice.example. CSP enforcement is on for code apps. Which two settings should Dana add?

options.A: https://api.fieldlink.example in connect-src.
options.B: https://intranet.cedarservice.example in frame-ancestors.
options.C: * in connect-src.
options.D: Turn enforcement off and keep reporting on.

items.signal: "call an API" → connect-src; "be embedded in" → frame-ancestors.
items.why: connect-src lists the origins the app may call; frame-ancestors lists the pages that may embed the app. Add exactly those origins.

distractors.C: A wildcard lets the app call any origin.
distractors.D: Removes the protection instead of configuring it.
distractors.E: frame-src controls what the app itself may frame, not who may frame the app.

items.stem: Lina wants other teams' flows and Azure services to react when Cedar marks a site as unsafe, without Cedar knowing who subscribes. The event carries SiteId and Reason. What should Karim create?

options.A: A custom API cedar_OnSiteMarkedUnsafe with a plug-in that updates the site.
options.B: A synchronous plug-in that calls each subscriber's webhook.
options.C: A custom API cedar_OnSiteMarkedUnsafe with no plug-in type, allowed step type Async Only, request parameters SiteId and Reason, and a catalog assignment in a catalog category.
options.D: The same custom API with allowed step type Sync and Async.

items.signal: "others react", "without knowing subscribers": a business event.
items.why: A business event is a custom API without a plug-in, Async Only, with request parameters only, published in the catalog; subscribers use "When an action is performed", asynchronous steps or service endpoints.

distractors.A: An event has no main-operation plug-in; it only announces that something happened.
distractors.B: Cedar would have to know and call every subscriber, inside the save.
distractors.D: Business events must be Async Only so subscribers can't slow down or roll back the save.

items.stem: CedarReports, LedgerLine and the FieldLink gateway must each receive work-order completions, and any of them may be offline for hours. Karim registers the Dataverse side with the Plug-in Registration Tool. Which two should he use?

options.A: One service endpoint with designation Topic and message format JSON, registered from a SAS connection string with Send rights.
options.B: One subscription per consumer on that Service Bus topic.
options.C: Three queue endpoints, one per consumer.
options.D: A SAS policy with Listen rights for the service endpoint.

items.signal: "three consumers", "offline for hours": one topic, a subscription each.
items.why: Dataverse posts once to a topic; each consumer reads its own subscription at its own pace, and messages wait while it is offline. Dataverse only sends, so the connection string needs Send.

distractors.C: It works, but three endpoints and three steps do what one topic does.
distractors.D: Dataverse only sends messages; Listen belongs to the consumers.
distractors.E: A webhook fails while its receiver is offline.

items.stem: On the Work orders main grid, a modern command "Send to FieldLink" must be visible only when exactly one row is selected, and must call cedar.workOrder.send with that row's ID. What should Karim configure?

options.A: Visible formula that tests Self.Selected.Item only; action Run JavaScript with no parameters.
options.B: Visible formula CountRows(Self.Selected.AllItems) = 1; action Run JavaScript with library cedar_/js/workorder.js, function cedar.workOrder.send and parameter SelectedControlSelectedItemIds.
options.C: The same visibility, and no execute privilege on the API because hidden buttons can't be clicked.
options.D: Edit the classic Send command in the command designer.

items.signal: "exactly one row" → AllItems count; "with that row's ID" → a parameter.
items.why: Self.Selected.AllItems counts the selection; the JavaScript action names one library and function and passes SelectedControlSelectedItemIds.

distractors.A: Item doesn't tell you how many rows are selected, and the function gets no ID.
distractors.C: Hiding a button isn't security; the API still needs its own check.
distractors.D: Classic commands can't be edited in the command designer.

items.stem: An HTTP-triggered Azure Function rebuilds a contract's 2,000 maintenance visits, which takes about six minutes. A cloud flow calls it and fails after about four minutes. What should Karim change?

options.A: Raise functionTimeout in host.json to ten minutes.
options.B: Return 200 immediately and continue the work in the same invocation.
options.C: Use a Durable Functions orchestrator that calls the Dataverse Web API directly.
options.D: An HTTP starter that returns 202 with a status URL; a Durable Functions orchestrator runs the rebuild in activity chunks; the flow follows the asynchronous pattern.

items.signal: "HTTP-triggered", "minutes": the 230-second HTTP response limit.
items.why: An HTTP request must be answered within 230 seconds whatever functionTimeout says. Accept, return 202 with a status URL and do the work in Durable activities; the orchestrator stays deterministic and does no I/O.

distractors.A: The HTTP response limit still applies.
distractors.B: Work after the response isn't guaranteed to finish.
distractors.C: Orchestrators must not do I/O; activities call Dataverse.

items.stem: Importing CedarServiceCore 1.11 (managed) into Cedar-Test fails with missing dependencies: the custom connector FieldLink Jobs and the environment variable cedar_FieldLinkBaseUrl. What should Karim do?

options.A: Import CedarServiceCore as unmanaged.
options.B: Remove the connector from CedarServiceCore and import again.
options.C: Import the matching managed version of CedarConnectors first, then CedarServiceCore.
options.D: Create the connector and the variable by hand in Cedar-Test.

items.signal: "missing dependencies" naming components of the base solution: import order.
items.why: CedarConnectors holds the connectors and their environment variables and must be installed before CedarServiceCore; a managed solution depends on managed components.

distractors.A: Unmanaged imports in test hide the problem and break the layering.
distractors.B: Removing a needed component gets past the error by breaking the solution.
distractors.D: Hand-made unmanaged components don't satisfy the managed dependency.

items.stem: An e-mail step must show Scheduled for (UTC, from the Dataverse trigger) in Amman time as "dd MMM yyyy HH:mm", or the text "not scheduled" when the column is empty. Which expression is correct?

options.A: if(empty(triggerOutputs()?['body/cedar_scheduledfor']), 'not scheduled', convertFromUtc(triggerOutputs()?['body/cedar_scheduledfor'], 'Jordan Standard Time', 'dd MMM yyyy HH:mm'))
options.B: formatDateTime(addHours(triggerOutputs()?['body/cedar_scheduledfor'], 3), 'dd MMM yyyy HH:mm')
options.C: if(equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/cedar_scheduledfor'], ''), 'not scheduled', convertFromUtc(triggerOutputs()?['body/cedar_scheduledfor'], 'Jordan Standard Time', 'dd MMM yyyy HH:mm'))
options.D: convertTimeZone(triggerOutputs()?['body/cedar_scheduledfor'], 'UTC', 'Amman', 'dd MMM yyyy HH:mm')

items.signal: "empty column" (null) and "local time with a format".
items.why: empty() is true for null; convertFromUtc takes a Windows time zone name and a format string. The ? operator avoids a failure when the property is missing.

distractors.B: A hard-coded offset is wrong whenever the zone's rules change, and an empty value fails.
distractors.C: An empty column arrives as null, which isn't equal to an empty string.
distractors.D: Amman isn't a time zone name the function accepts, and an empty value fails.

items.stem: The field control cedar.SitePhotos must let coordinators take a photo with the device camera in the mobile app, and must show its Upload button only when the user can create notes. What should Karim do?

options.A: Call context.device.captureImage without declaring anything.
options.B: Use context.mode.isControlDisabled to decide whether the user can create notes.
options.C: Declare Device.captureImage and WebAPI in feature-usage; call context.utils.getEntityMetadata("annotation"), then context.utils.hasEntityPrivilege before showing Upload.
options.D: Use navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia directly.

items.signal: "device camera" (declared feature) and "can create notes" (privilege check).
items.why: Device and Web API features must be declared in the manifest. hasEntityPrivilege answers the privilege question once the table's metadata is loaded with getEntityMetadata.

distractors.A: Undeclared features aren't available at runtime.
distractors.B: isControlDisabled says whether the control is read-only, not whether the user may create notes.
distractors.D: Bypasses the framework; it isn't the supported way and may not work in the mobile app.

items.stem: The plug-in SiteRiskPlugin must read files from the Azure Storage container site-risk without storing any secret. What should Karim set up?

options.A: Put the storage account key in the step's secure configuration.
options.B: Create an application user for the storage account in the environment.
options.C: Post the request to Service Bus with IServiceEndpointNotificationService and read the files elsewhere.
options.D: Sign the assembly, create a user-assigned managed identity with a federated credential for the plug-in, bind a managedidentities record to the assembly, grant Storage Blob Data Reader, and get tokens through IManagedIdentityService.

items.signal: "plug-in calls Azure", "no secret": Power Platform managed identity for plug-ins.
items.why: A plug-in assembly linked to a managed identity gets Azure tokens through IManagedIdentityService. Federated credentials (version 2 subject) replace secrets; the identity needs only the Azure role for the container.

distractors.A: Secure configuration still stores a secret, which the requirement rules out.
distractors.B: An application user lets something call Dataverse; this is the other direction.
distractors.C: It moves the problem elsewhere instead of letting the plug-in read the files.

items.stem: In the FieldLink Jobs connector, the CreateJob parameter subcontractorCode should show a list of current subcontractors returned by the operation ListSubcontractors (array items, fields code and name). The list changes every week. What should Karim add to the OpenAPI definition?

options.A: An enum with the current codes on subcontractorCode.
options.B: x-ms-summary: "Subcontractor" on subcontractorCode.
options.C: x-ms-visibility: internal with a default value on subcontractorCode.
options.D: x-ms-dynamic-values on subcontractorCode with operationId ListSubcontractors, value-collection items, value-path code and value-title name.

items.signal: "list from another operation", "changes every week": dynamic values.
items.why: x-ms-dynamic-values fills a parameter's list at design time by calling another operation; value-collection, value-path and value-title select the array and the fields.

distractors.A: A static list would be out of date within a week.
distractors.B: x-ms-summary only sets the label.
distractors.C: Hides the parameter and fixes one value.

items.stem: The Dispatch Planner's start page reads 120 work orders, then sends one request per work order to read its site (121 requests), and takes 9 seconds to become interactive. What should Karim change first?

options.A: Read the sites in one request filtered by the distinct site IDs, keep them in a session cache, and run independent loads in parallel.
options.B: Raise the page size to 5,000 rows.
options.C: Store the sites in localStorage permanently.
options.D: Rewrite the queries in FetchXML.

items.signal: "one request per row": an N+1 pattern.
items.why: Replacing N+1 calls with one batched read removes most of the latency; caching for the session and parallel independent loads cut the rest.

distractors.B: The page size isn't what makes 121 requests.
distractors.C: Persistent browser storage of customer data is a privacy risk and goes stale.
distractors.D: FetchXML isn't supported in code apps, and the language isn't the problem.

items.stem: Cedar Service Assistant (Copilot Studio) must hand dispatch questions to cedar-dispatch-advisor, a Foundry agent owned by another team with its own release cycle. How should Karim connect them?

options.A: Add cedar-dispatch-advisor as a child agent of Cedar Service Assistant.
options.B: Add it as a connected agent through Add an agent → Microsoft Foundry (preview), after the Foundry agent is enabled for the Activity protocol.
options.C: Copy the Foundry agent's instructions into a topic of Cedar Service Assistant.
options.D: Call the Foundry agent from a cloud flow with an HTTP action and a stored key.

items.signal: "another team", "own release cycle", "Foundry": a connected agent.
items.why: Connected agents keep their own lifecycle and owner; Copilot Studio can connect to a Foundry agent (preview) once that agent exposes the Activity protocol. Child agents are for work the same team releases together.

distractors.A: Child agents live inside the main agent and are released with it.
distractors.C: A copy drifts from the real agent and loses its tools.
distractors.D: Stores a key and bypasses the supported connection.

items.stem: Releases to Cedar-Prod must wait for Lina's approval and may be deployed only between 18:00 and 20:00 Amman time. Makers have no rights in Cedar-Prod. What should Karim configure in Power Platform Pipelines?

options.A: Delegated deployment with a service principal on the production stage (which requires approval), and a pre-deployment step whose handler lets the deployment continue only inside the window.
options.B: Give makers the System Customizer role in Cedar-Prod and let them deploy as themselves.
options.C: Use the deployment-completed notification to roll back releases deployed outside the window.
options.D: Add Cedar-Prod as a target without making it a Managed Environment.

items.signal: "approval", "no rights in production", "only in a window".
items.why: Delegated deployment runs as a service principal or stage owner and always waits for approval; a pre-deployment step runs after approval, just before import, so a handler can hold the deployment until the window.

distractors.B: Gives makers production rights, which the stem rules out.
distractors.C: A notification after deployment can't prevent it.
distractors.D: Pipeline targets must be Managed Environments.

items.stem: Solution: the job sends ExecuteMultipleRequest batches of 500 UpsertRequest messages keyed by cedar_invoicenumber with ContinueOnError = true, from as many parallel tasks as ServiceClient.RecommendedDegreesOfParallelism suggests, and logs the faulted responses. Does the solution meet the goal?

options.A: Yes
options.B: No

items.signal: "create missing", "one bad row mustn't stop the others", "faster": keyed upserts with per-request verdicts, in parallel.
items.why: Upserts create missing invoice numbers; ExecuteMultiple runs each request in its own transaction and, with ContinueOnError, reports each failure without stopping the batch; parallel batches at the recommended degree of parallelism cut the time.

distractors.B: Every part of the goal is met: creation, isolation of failures and throughput.

items.stem: Solution: the job keeps one UpdateRequest per row but runs 64 parallel tasks, and retries a request immediately, up to five times, when it receives a service protection error. Does the solution meet the goal?

options.A: Yes
options.B: No

items.signal: "immediately" after a service protection error, and still UpdateRequest.
items.why: Service protection errors carry Retry-After; retrying immediately only meets more 429s, and 64 tasks exceed the concurrent-request limit for one user. UpdateRequest also still fails for missing invoice numbers.

distractors.A: Three parts of the goal fail: missing rows aren't created, immediate retries ignore Retry-After, and the concurrency exceeds the limit.

items.stem: Solution: the job sends UpsertMultipleRequest batches of 1,000 rows from eight parallel tasks and logs every batch that fails. Does the solution meet the goal?

options.A: Yes
options.B: No

items.signal: "never let one bad row stop the others" on a standard table.
items.why: UpsertMultiple is fast, but on standard tables any error rolls back the whole request: one bad row fails 999 good ones. ExecuteMultiple or smaller batches with a fallback are needed for per-row isolation.

distractors.A: It is fast and creates missing rows, but one bad row stops its whole batch of 1,000.

items.stem: Requirement 1: which call should the command's JavaScript make after the agent confirms?

options.A: Xrm.WebApi.updateRecord("incident", id, { cedar_escalate: true })
options.B: fetch() to /api/data/v9.2/incidents(<id>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.cedar_EscalateCase with a bearer token kept in the web resource.
options.C: Xrm.WebApi.online.execute(request), where request.getMetadata() returns boundParameter "entity", the parameter entity of type mscrm.incident, operationType 0 and operationName "cedar_EscalateCase".
options.D: The same execute call with operationType 1.

items.signal: "call the existing custom API", bound action, from a form script.
items.why: Xrm.WebApi.online.execute runs custom APIs as the signed-in user. A bound API takes the parameter named entity with its type, and operationType 0 marks an action (1 is a function, 2 a CRUD operation).

distractors.A: It changes a column instead of calling the API; nothing in the stem reacts to such a column.
distractors.B: A token in a web resource is a secret in client code; Xrm.WebApi already authenticates as the user.
distractors.D: 1 means function, which is called with GET; cedar_EscalateCase is an action.

items.stem: Requirement 2: how should Cedar Night Desk talk to Cedar Service Assistant?

options.A: The Copilot Studio client library (Microsoft 365 Agents SDK) with the environment ID and the agent's schema name, using a delegated token with CopilotStudio.Copilots.Invoke for the signed-in supervisor.
options.B: The same client library with an app-only token from the web app's managed identity.
options.C: Call the Dataverse MCP server directly from the web app and skip the agent.
options.D: Embed the agent's web chat with authentication set to No authentication.

items.signal: "signed-in supervisor", "limited to what that supervisor may see": a delegated client-library call.
items.why: The client library talks to a published agent with a user token carrying CopilotStudio.Copilots.Invoke, so the agent's knowledge and tools act for that supervisor.

distractors.B: The client library doesn't accept service principal (app-only) tokens.
distractors.C: It bypasses the agent the requirement names, with its instructions and tools.
distractors.D: Without authentication the agent can't act as the supervisor, and anyone with the page can use it.

items.stem: Requirement 3: how should the CedarReports loader read cases?

options.A: Query cases with modifiedon greater than the last run time.
options.B: A Service Bus queue endpoint on Create, Update and Delete of incident, read by the loader.
options.C: Change tracking with $filter=modifiedon gt <last run> to keep the response small.
options.D: Enable Track changes on Case; the first request uses Prefer: odata.track-changes with $select; store the @odata.deltaLink and follow it every 15 minutes, deleting rows reported as $deletedEntity.

items.signal: "own copy", "deleted rows", "paused for three days".
items.why: Change tracking returns changed and deleted rows since the last delta token. Three days are within the default retention of seven days; apply the changes, then store the new delta link.

distractors.A: Deleted cases never appear in a modifiedon query.
distractors.B: It works, but adds an endpoint, steps and ordering problems for something change tracking already provides.
distractors.C: Change tracking requests refuse $filter.

items.stem: Requirement 4: what should Karim set up?

options.A: A Power Platform Monitor alert rule on the Cedar Operations app.
options.B: An Azure Monitor log search alert on appi-cedar-prod: a KQL query over customEvents named EscalationFailed in the last 15 minutes, threshold more than 5, evaluated every 5 minutes, returning the case numbers, with an action group that notifies Lina.
options.C: The Dataverse export to Application Insights with an alert on failed plug-in executions.
options.D: A cloud flow that e-mails Lina for each failed page.

items.signal: "within 10 minutes", "more than five in 15 minutes", "which cases": own telemetry and a log search alert.
items.why: The function's own custom events arrive within minutes; a log search alert evaluates the threshold over a window every few minutes and can include the case numbers in its results.

distractors.A: Monitor alerts are evaluated daily on product metrics: far too late, and they don't know case numbers.
distractors.C: The admin export has a delivery time of up to 24 hours, and plug-in failures aren't the paging failures.
distractors.D: It sends a message per failure instead of alerting on the threshold.

items.stem: Requirement 1: how should the command confirm and report?

options.A: window.confirm() before the call and window.alert() with the result.
options.B: Xrm.Navigation.openConfirmDialog; when the result has confirmed true, call the API, then formContext.ui.setFormNotification with the EscalationId.
options.C: Xrm.Navigation.openAlertDialog to ask, then call the API.
options.D: Xrm.Navigation.openForm to a confirmation form, then return to the case.

items.signal: "ask for confirmation", "show the result without leaving the form".
items.why: openConfirmDialog resolves with { confirmed }; a form notification shows the outcome on the same form.

distractors.A: Browser dialogs aren't supported in model-driven apps and block the page.
distractors.C: An alert dialog has only OK: it can't be declined.
distractors.D: Opening another form leaves the case, risking unsaved changes.
